headline: Indian markets end September with worst monthly performance since March amid global headwinds and FII outflows

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Global rate hikes and rising crude oil prices sparked significant FII outflows from Indian benchmark shares
Benchmark indices logged their worst monthly performance since March due to global economic pressures
Markets failed to hold onto intraday gains amid persistent volatility and global headwinds
Concerns over high bond yields and international market instability impacted investor sentiment throughout September
whatHappening: The Indian rupee rebounded to 95.83 against the US dollar as international crude prices eased
The Indian government slashed export duties on diesel and aviation turbine fuel while keeping petrol unchanged
Sensex and Nifty recorded their worst nine-month performance in 15 years following a weak September close
Aurobindo Pharma's subsidiary Acrotech entered the US dermatology market with the launch of Adquey
summary: Indian markets ended September with their worst monthly performance since March, driven by global rate hikes and FII outflows. Despite the volatility, the Indian rupee saw a slight rebound as crude oil prices eased and the government adjusted fuel export duties. Aurobindo Pharma provided a positive corporate highlight by expanding its presence in the US dermatology market.
